title: 蜀道难
title_en: Hard Is the Road to Shu
author: 李白

form.zh: 乐府诗（七言为主的杂言古诗）
form.en: yuefu song (an old-style poem of mixed line lengths, mostly seven characters)

text_note.zh: 这里用的是现在课本里的文字。原始文字开头写作“噫吁戏”，课本作“噫吁嚱”，都是惊叹声。“猨”“劒”是“猿”“剑”的旧写法；“砅厓”课本作“砯崖”，指水冲击山崖。另外，课本把“蜀道之难难于上青天”分成两句。
text_note.en: This is the text taught in schools today. The source writes the opening cry with a different last character; textbooks use the one read xī. Both are just sounds of amazement. The words for "ape" and "sword" appear in older forms in the source. The source's phrase for water striking the cliffs uses different characters; textbooks write it pīng yá. Textbooks also split the refrain "the road to Shu is hard, harder than climbing the blue sky" into two lines.

readings.en: A cry of amazement, read xū.

readings.zh: 课本注音 xī，也是惊叹声。
readings.en: Read xī, as textbooks mark it. It is also a cry of amazement.

readings.zh: 险要的关口，读 sài，不读 sāi 或 sè。
readings.en: Meaning a guarded mountain pass, read sài, not sāi or sè.
Meaning to fly across, read guò.

readings.zh: 这里是星宿名“参宿”，读 shēn，不读 cān。
readings.en: Here it is the name of a star group, read shēn, not cān.
Meaning to come back, read huán, not hái.

readings.zh: 大声哀叫，读 háo，不读 hào。
readings.en: Meaning to wail, read háo, not hào.

readings.zh: 水冲击山崖的声音，读 pīng。
readings.en: The sound of water crashing on rock, read pīng.

readings.zh: “胡为”就是“为什么”，课本读 wèi；也有人读 wéi。
readings.en: Hú wèi means "why". Textbooks read it wèi; some people read it wéi.
Meaning morning, read zhāo, not cháo.
Meaning happy, read lè, not yuè.
Meaning to return, read huán, not hái.

glosses.zh: 噫吁嚱：惊叹的声音，相当于“哎呀呀”。
glosses.en: yī xū xī: a cry of amazement, like "Oh, oh, oh!"

glosses.zh: 危乎高哉：多么高啊！危，高。乎、哉，都是表示感叹的字。
glosses.en: wēi hū gāo zāi: how high it is! Wēi means high. Hū and zāi are words that show strong feeling.

glosses.zh: 蜀道：从长安一带进入蜀地（今天四川）的山路。蜀，今天的四川一带。
glosses.en: shǔ dào: the mountain roads from the Chang'an region into Shu. Shu is the area of today's Sichuan.

glosses.zh: 难于上青天：比登上青天还难。于，比。
glosses.en: nán yú shàng qīng tiān: harder than climbing up to the blue sky. Yú here means "than".

glosses.zh: 蚕丛、鱼凫：传说中古代蜀国最早的两位国王。及，和。
glosses.en: cán cóng, yú fú: Cancong and Yufu, two of the first kings of ancient Shu in legend. Jí means "and".

glosses.zh: 何茫然：多么渺茫、模糊啊，意思是年代太久远，事情说不清了。
glosses.en: hé máng rán: how dim and unclear! It was so long ago that nobody can say what happened.

glosses.zh: 尔来：从那时以来。
glosses.en: ěr lái: since that time.

glosses.zh: 四万八千岁：四万八千年，夸张地说时间很长。
glosses.en: sì wàn bā qiān suì: forty-eight thousand years, an exaggeration meaning a very long time.

glosses.zh: 秦塞：秦地，指今天陕西一带。塞，险要的地方。
glosses.en: qín sài: the land of Qin, today's Shaanxi. Sài is a guarded, rugged place.

glosses.zh: 通人烟：人们来往。人烟，有人住的地方冒出的炊烟，代指人。
glosses.en: tōng rén yān: people going back and forth. Rén yān is the smoke of cooking fires, a sign that people live there.

glosses.zh: 西当：西边对着。当，对着。
glosses.en: xī dāng: facing west. Dāng means to face.

glosses.zh: 太白：太白山，秦岭的最高峰，在长安西边。
glosses.en: tài bái: Mount Taibai, the highest peak of the Qinling Mountains, west of Chang'an.

glosses.zh: 鸟道：只有鸟才能飞过的窄道。
glosses.en: niǎo dào: a narrow way that only birds can fly through.

glosses.zh: 横绝：横着飞越过去。
glosses.en: héng jué: to fly straight across.

glosses.zh: 峨眉巅：峨眉山的山顶。峨眉山在今天四川。
glosses.en: é méi diān: the top of Mount Emei, in today's Sichuan.

glosses.zh: 地崩山摧壮士死：传说秦王送五个美女给蜀王，蜀王派五个大力士去接。回来路上遇见一条大蛇钻进山洞，五人一起拉蛇，结果山崩了，大力士和美女都被压死，山也分成了五座岭。摧，倒塌。
glosses.en: dì bēng shān cuī zhuàng shì sǐ: a legend. The King of Qin sent five beauties to the King of Shu, who sent five strongmen to fetch them. On the way back a huge snake slid into a cave. The five men pulled it out together, the mountain fell, and everyone was crushed. The mountain split into five ridges. Cuī means to collapse.

glosses.zh: 天梯：像通到天上的梯子一样的山路。
glosses.en: tiān tī: a mountain path as steep as a ladder to the sky.

glosses.zh: 石栈：栈道，在悬崖上凿孔、架木头修成的路。
glosses.en: shí zhàn: a plank road, made by cutting holes in a cliff and laying wooden beams across them.

glosses.zh: 相钩连：互相连接起来。
glosses.en: xiāng gōu lián: hooked together, joined up.

glosses.zh: 六龙回日：神话说太阳神坐着六条龙拉的车，每天在天上走。这里说山太高，连太阳车也只能掉头回去。
glosses.en: liù lóng huí rì: in myth, the sun rides a chariot pulled by six dragons across the sky. Here the mountains are so high that even the sun's chariot has to turn back.

glosses.zh: 高标：最高的山峰，高得像标杆一样。
glosses.en: gāo biāo: the highest peak, standing up like a marker pole.

glosses.zh: 冲波逆折：激流冲击，翻卷着倒流回来。
glosses.en: chōng bō nì zhé: rushing waves that crash and twist back on themselves.

glosses.zh: 回川：打着旋儿的河流。
glosses.en: huí chuān: a river full of whirlpools.

glosses.zh: 黄鹤：黄鹄，一种很会飞的大鸟。
glosses.en: huáng hè: a great yellow crane, a bird that flies high and far.

glosses.zh: 尚不得过：还飞不过去。尚，还。
glosses.en: shàng bù dé guò: still cannot fly over. Shàng means "even, still".

glosses.zh: 猿猱：猿和猴子，最会攀爬。猱，一种猴子。
glosses.en: yuán náo: apes and monkeys, the best climbers. Náo is a kind of monkey.

glosses.zh: 欲度：想要越过去。
glosses.en: yù dù: want to get across.

glosses.zh: 愁攀援：发愁怎么往上爬。攀援，抓着东西往上爬。
glosses.en: chóu pān yuán: worry about how to climb. Pān yuán means to climb by grabbing hold.

glosses.zh: 青泥：青泥岭，在今天甘肃和陕西交界的地方，是进蜀的要道。
glosses.en: qīng ní: the Qingni Ridge, on today's border of Gansu and Shaanxi, a main road into Shu.

glosses.zh: 盘盘：弯弯曲曲、绕来绕去的样子。
glosses.en: pán pán: winding round and round.

glosses.zh: 百步九折：走一百步要拐九个弯。
glosses.en: bǎi bù jiǔ zhé: nine turns in every hundred steps.

glosses.zh: 萦岩峦：绕着山岩和山峰转。萦，盘绕。
glosses.en: yíng yán luán: winding around the rocks and peaks. Yíng means to coil around.

glosses.zh: 扪参历井：参、井是天上的两组星宿，古人把参对应蜀地，井对应秦地。这里说山高得伸手就能摸到星星，从星星旁边走过。扪，摸。历，经过。
glosses.en: mén shēn lì jǐng: Shen and Jing are two star groups. The ancients linked Shen to Shu and Jing to Qin. The mountain is so high you can touch the stars and walk past them. Mén means to touch; lì means to pass by.

glosses.zh: 仰胁息：仰着头，憋住气不敢喘。胁息，屏住呼吸。
glosses.en: yǎng xié xī: looking up and holding your breath in fear.

glosses.zh: 抚膺：摸着胸口。膺，胸。
glosses.en: fǔ yīng: pressing a hand to the chest. Yīng means chest.

glosses.zh: 坐长叹：徒然长长地叹气。坐，空、徒然。
glosses.en: zuò cháng tàn: sighing long and helplessly. Zuò here means "in vain", not "to sit".

glosses.zh: 君：你，指入蜀的朋友。
glosses.en: jūn: you, the friend going into Shu.

glosses.zh: 畏途：让人害怕的路。
glosses.en: wèi tú: a road that makes you afraid.

glosses.zh: 巉岩：又高又陡的山岩。
glosses.en: chán yán: tall, steep rocks.

glosses.zh: 号古木：在老树上哀叫。号，大声哭叫。
glosses.en: háo gǔ mù: crying out in old trees. Háo means to wail.

glosses.zh: 雄飞雌从：雄鸟在前面飞，雌鸟在后面跟着。
glosses.en: xióng fēi cí cóng: the male bird flies ahead and the female follows.

glosses.zh: 子规：杜鹃鸟，叫声很悲哀，像在说“不如归去”。
glosses.en: zǐ guī: the cuckoo. Its call sounds sad, and people heard it as "better go home".

glosses.zh: 愁空山：在空荡荡的山里叫得人发愁。
glosses.en: chóu kōng shān: its calls fill the empty mountains with sorrow.

glosses.zh: 凋朱颜：红润的脸色变得憔悴，像花凋谢一样。朱颜，红润的脸，指年轻的容貌。
glosses.en: diāo zhū yán: a rosy young face turns pale and worn, like a flower wilting. Zhū yán means a rosy face, youth.

glosses.zh: 去天不盈尺：离天不到一尺。去，离。盈，满。
glosses.en: qù tiān bù yíng chǐ: less than a foot from the sky. Qù means "away from"; yíng means "full".

glosses.zh: 倚绝壁：靠在陡峭的悬崖上。
glosses.en: yǐ jué bì: leaning on a sheer cliff.

glosses.zh: 飞湍：飞奔的急流。
glosses.en: fēi tuān: a racing, rushing stream.

glosses.zh: 喧豗：轰隆隆的巨大声响。
glosses.en: xuān huī: a great roaring noise.

glosses.zh: 砯崖：水冲击山崖。砯，水撞石头的声音。
glosses.en: pīng yá: water crashing against the cliffs. Pīng is the sound of water hitting rock.

glosses.zh: 转石：冲得石头翻滚。
glosses.en: zhuǎn shí: sending rocks tumbling.

glosses.zh: 万壑雷：千万条山谷里响起雷一样的声音。壑，山谷。
glosses.en: wàn hè léi: thunder in ten thousand valleys. Hè means a valley.

glosses.zh: 嗟：唉，叹气声。
glosses.en: jiē: alas, a sigh.

glosses.zh: 尔：你。
glosses.en: ěr: you.

glosses.zh: 胡为乎来哉：为什么要来呢？胡为，为什么。
glosses.en: hú wèi hū lái zāi: why would you come here? Hú wèi means "why".

glosses.zh: 剑阁：又叫剑门关，在今天四川剑阁县北，是进蜀的重要关口。
glosses.en: jiàn gé: Jiange, also called the Sword Gate Pass, north of today's Jiange County in Sichuan, a key gateway into Shu.

glosses.zh: 峥嵘、崔嵬：都是山又高又险的样子。
glosses.en: zhēng róng, cuī wéi: both describe mountains that are tall and rugged.

glosses.zh: 一夫当关：一个人守住关口。当，守着、挡着。
glosses.en: yī fū dāng guān: one man guarding the pass. Dāng means to stand in the way.

glosses.zh: 万夫莫开：一万个人也打不开。莫，不能。
glosses.en: wàn fū mò kāi: ten thousand men cannot break through. Mò means "cannot".

glosses.zh: 所守或匪亲：守关的人如果不是可靠的人。匪，同“非”，不是。亲，亲信。
glosses.en: suǒ shǒu huò fěi qīn: if the people guarding it are not trustworthy. Fěi means "not"; qīn means a trusted person.

glosses.zh: 化为狼与豺：就会变成狼和豺一样的坏人，起来作乱。
glosses.en: huà wéi láng yǔ chái: they will turn into wolves and jackals and rise up in revolt.

glosses.zh: 朝：早晨。
glosses.en: zhāo: in the morning.

glosses.zh: 长蛇：大蛇。猛虎、长蛇也比喻凶狠的坏人。
glosses.en: cháng shé: a great snake. Fierce tigers and great snakes also stand for cruel, violent people.

glosses.zh: 吮血：吸血。
glosses.en: shǔn xuè: sucking blood.

glosses.zh: 杀人如麻：杀的人像乱麻一样多，数也数不清。
glosses.en: shā rén rú má: killing people as thick as a tangle of hemp, too many to count.

glosses.zh: 锦城：锦官城，就是今天的四川成都。
glosses.en: jǐn chéng: the Brocade City, today's Chengdu in Sichuan.

glosses.zh: 虽云乐：虽然说是快乐的地方。云，说。
glosses.en: suī yún lè: although people say it is a happy place. Yún means "to say".

glosses.zh: 侧身：侧着身子，形容害怕、不安。
glosses.en: cè shēn: turning sideways, a sign of fear and unease.

glosses.zh: 咨嗟：叹气。
glosses.en: zī jiē: to sigh.

translation.zh: 哎呀呀！
translation.en: Oh, oh, oh!

translation.zh: 多么高啊！
translation.en: How high, how steep!

translation.zh: 蜀道太难走了，
translation.en: The road to Shu is so hard,

translation.zh: 比登上青天还难！
translation.en: harder than climbing up to the blue sky!

translation.zh: 蚕丛和鱼凫两位古代蜀王，
translation.en: Cancong and Yufu, the old kings of Shu,

translation.zh: 他们建国的事多么久远，已经说不清了。
translation.en: founded their land so long ago that it is all a blur.

translation.zh: 从那以后过了四万八千年，
translation.en: For forty-eight thousand years after that,

translation.zh: 蜀地和秦地都没有人来往。
translation.en: no people went back and forth between Shu and Qin.

translation.zh: 西边对着太白山，只有一条鸟才飞得过的小道，
translation.en: To the west, Mount Taibai has only a path for birds,

translation.zh: 鸟儿能从那里一直飞到峨眉山顶。
translation.en: and birds can fly straight across it to the top of Mount Emei.

translation.zh: 直到山崩地裂，压死了五位壮士，
translation.en: Then the earth split and the mountains fell, crushing the five strongmen,

translation.zh: 这才有了天梯和石栈一段段连起来。
translation.en: and only after that were sky ladders and plank roads joined together.

translation.zh: 上面有连太阳神的六龙车都要掉头的高峰，
translation.en: Above rise peaks so high that the sun's six-dragon chariot must turn back,

translation.zh: 下面有激浪翻滚、打着旋的河流。
translation.en: and below run rivers of crashing, swirling waves.

translation.zh: 善飞的黄鹤都飞不过去，
translation.en: Even the yellow crane, strong in flight, cannot get over,

translation.zh: 最会爬的猿猴想过去也发愁怎么攀爬。
translation.en: and apes and monkeys, wanting to cross, worry how to climb.

translation.zh: 青泥岭的山路多么曲折，
translation.en: How the Qingni Ridge road winds and winds,

translation.zh: 走一百步拐九个弯，绕着山岩转。
translation.en: nine turns in a hundred steps, coiling round the rocks.

translation.zh: 伸手摸到星星，从星星旁走过，仰着头不敢喘气，
translation.en: You touch the stars and pass them by, looking up and holding your breath,

translation.zh: 只能摸着胸口，坐着长长地叹气。
translation.en: then press your hand to your chest and sigh long and hopelessly.

translation.zh: 请问你这次西去，什么时候回来？
translation.en: Tell me, friend, going west, when will you come back?

translation.zh: 这条可怕的路上全是高险的山岩，没法攀登。
translation.en: This fearful road is all sheer rock that no one can climb.

translation.zh: 只看见悲哀的鸟在老树上哀叫，
translation.en: You will only see sad birds crying in the ancient trees,

translation.zh: 雄鸟在前飞，雌鸟在后跟，绕着林子转。
translation.en: the male flying ahead, the female following, circling the woods.

translation.zh: 又听见杜鹃在月夜里啼叫，
translation.en: And you will hear the cuckoo calling under the night moon,

translation.zh: 叫得空山里一片哀愁。
translation.en: filling the empty mountains with sorrow.

translation.zh: 蜀道太难走了，
translation.en: The road to Shu is so hard,

translation.zh: 比登上青天还难，
translation.en: harder than climbing up to the blue sky,

translation.zh: 让人一听就愁得红润的脸色都憔悴了！
translation.en: that just hearing of it makes rosy young faces wither!

translation.zh: 连绵的山峰离天不到一尺，
translation.en: Peak after peak stands less than a foot from the sky,

translation.zh: 干枯的松树倒挂在陡峭的悬崖上。
translation.en: and dead pines hang upside down from the sheer cliffs.

translation.zh: 飞奔的急流和瀑布争着发出轰响，
translation.en: Racing streams and waterfalls roar as if competing,

translation.zh: 冲击山崖、推着石头翻滚，千万条山谷像在打雷。
translation.en: beating on the cliffs, rolling the rocks, like thunder in ten thousand valleys.

translation.zh: 这里就是这样险，
translation.en: So dangerous is this place:

translation.zh: 唉，你这远方的人为什么要来这里呢？
translation.en: alas, you who come from far away, why would you come here at all?

translation.zh: 剑阁高大险峻，
translation.en: Jiange Pass towers high and rugged:

translation.zh: 一个人守住关口，
translation.en: one man guarding the pass

translation.zh: 一万个人也打不进来。
translation.en: can hold off ten thousand.

translation.zh: 守关的人如果不是可靠的人，
translation.en: If those who guard it cannot be trusted,

translation.zh: 就会变成豺狼一样作乱。
translation.en: they will turn into wolves and jackals.

translation.zh: 早上要躲猛虎，
translation.en: In the morning you must hide from fierce tigers,

translation.zh: 晚上要躲大蛇。
translation.en: at night from great snakes,

translation.zh: 它们磨着牙齿吸人血，
translation.en: grinding their teeth and sucking blood,

translation.zh: 杀死的人多得像乱麻。
translation.en: killing people beyond counting.

translation.zh: 锦官城虽然说是个快乐的地方，
translation.en: Though the Brocade City is said to be a happy place,

translation.zh: 还不如早点回家。
translation.en: you would do better to come home early.

translation.zh: 蜀道太难走了，
translation.en: The road to Shu is so hard,

translation.zh: 比登上青天还难，
translation.en: harder than climbing up to the blue sky,

translation.zh: 我侧着身子向西望去，长长地叹气。
translation.en: I turn and gaze west, and sigh a long, long sigh.

background.zh: 《蜀道难》是一个乐府旧题，就是古代早就有的歌曲题目，前人用它写过蜀道的艰险。一般认为这首诗写在唐玄宗天宝初年李白在长安的时候，一说写于更早的开元年间。据唐人孟棨《本事诗》记载，贺知章读了这首诗，惊叹不已，称李白是“谪仙人”，意思是从天上被贬到人间的神仙。至于为什么写这首诗，说法很多：一说是送朋友入蜀，一说是暗中批评当时的政局，一说只是借古题描写蜀道的险。
background.en: "Hard Is the Road to Shu" is an old yuefu title, a song title used long before Li Bai, and earlier poets used it to write about the dangerous roads into Shu. The poem is usually dated to the early Tianbao years of Emperor Xuanzong, when Li Bai was in Chang'an; another view puts it earlier, in the Kaiyuan years. The Tang writer Meng Qi records that when He Zhizhang read it, he was amazed and called Li Bai "an immortal sent down from heaven". Why Li Bai wrote it is debated. Some say it sees off a friend going to Shu. Some say it quietly criticizes the politics of the time. Some say it simply uses the old title to show how dangerous the road was.

author_note.zh: 李白（701—762），字太白，号青莲居士，唐代最有名的诗人之一，被称为“诗仙”。他少年时在蜀地长大，熟悉那里的山川。他的诗想象大胆，常常用夸张和神话，句子长短自由，这首《蜀道难》就是最好的例子。
author_note.en: Li Bai (701–762), also called Taibai, is one of the most famous Tang poets, known as the Immortal of Poetry. He grew up in Shu as a boy and knew its mountains and rivers. His poems are full of bold imagination, exaggeration and myth, with lines of free length. This poem is one of the best examples.

appreciation.zh: 这首诗一开口就是一声“哎呀呀”，好像诗人站在山前被吓了一跳。接着他从远古讲起：蚕丛、鱼凫的传说，五丁开山的故事，让蜀道显得又古老又神秘。然后他用一连串夸张的画面写山高水险：太阳车要掉头，黄鹤飞不过，猿猴也发愁，伸手就能摸到星星。再写路上的凄凉：悲鸟、杜鹃、空山。最后写人的危险：剑阁一夫当关，守关的人可能作乱，还有猛虎长蛇。“蜀道之难，难于上青天”这句话出现了三次，像歌曲的副歌，一次比一次沉重。读的时候，句子忽长忽短，就像在山路上一会儿爬坡、一会儿转弯，让人跟着喘不过气来。
appreciation.en: The poem opens with a cry, "Oh, oh, oh!", as if the poet has been startled at the foot of the mountains. Then he goes back to ancient times: the old kings Cancong and Yufu, and the five strongmen who split the mountain. The road feels old and mysterious. Next comes a string of wild pictures of height and danger. The sun's chariot must turn back, the yellow crane cannot fly over, monkeys worry, and you can touch the stars. Then the loneliness of the road: sad birds, the cuckoo, empty mountains. Last, the danger from people: one man can hold Jiange Pass, the guards might rebel, and tigers and snakes wait. The line "the road to Shu is hard, harder than climbing the blue sky" comes three times, like a chorus, heavier each time. The lines jump between long and short, like a mountain path that climbs and then twists, and the reader runs out of breath along with it.
